home.editorBody: Kryptonews prints the crypto market the way a newspaper prints the stock pages: the 100 largest cryptocurrencies, updated every two minutes, set next to the headlines that move them. One page, no noise, no ads, no tracking.
home.editorBody2: Read the free edition as long as you like. Request a free account to unlock the whole ledger, clip stories into your scrapbook and keep an eye on the coins you care about.
home.empty: The presses are warming up: the first headlines arrive a few minutes after start-up.

what.a: Kryptonews is a free, ad-free crypto newspaper. It combines live prices for the 100 largest cryptocurrencies with headlines from English and French crypto newsrooms, in a single newspaper-style page.

data.q: Where do the prices come from?
data.a: Market data (prices, market capitalisation, volume, 1h/24h/7d change and charts) is provided by the CoinGecko API and stored on our server, so your browser never contacts CoinGecko directly.

refresh.q: How often is the data refreshed?
refresh.a: Prices are refreshed every two minutes, exchange rates every thirty minutes and news feeds every ten minutes. Each page shows when its data was last updated.

free.a: Yes. Visitors can read a free edition without an account. A free account unlocks the full list of coins and headlines, clippings (saved stories) and watched coins.

sources.a: In English: Cointelegraph, CoinDesk, Decrypt, The Block and Bitcoin Magazine. In French: Journal du Coin, Cryptoast and Coin Academy. Each headline links to the original article on the publisher's site.

advice.a: No. Kryptonews only reports information. Nothing on the site is a recommendation to buy or sell. Crypto-assets are highly volatile and you can lose all of your capital.

about.title: About Kryptonews
about.deck: A crypto newspaper that prints itself every two minutes.
about.what: Kryptonews is a free web application that brings together live prices for the 100 largest cryptocurrencies and headlines from English- and French-language crypto newsrooms. It is designed like a broadsheet: a front page, a market ledger, a news wire and a scrapbook of clippings.
about.data: Prices, market capitalisation, volume, 1h/24h/7d change, 7-day sparklines and historical charts come from the CoinGecko API. Headlines come from the public RSS feeds of each newsroom: Kryptonews shows the title, a short excerpt and a link to the original article, which remains the property of its publisher.
about.rhythm: Prices: every 2 minutes. Exchange rates (more than 50 currencies): every 30 minutes. News feeds: every 10 minutes. Headlines older than 45 days are deleted automatically (clippings keep their own copy).
about.privacy: No ads, no analytics, no tracking cookies. Fonts and images are served from our own server, so your browser never contacts third parties. Accounts only store what is needed to run them, and you can export or delete your data at any time.
about.history: Kryptonews started in 2023 as a group project in the Epitech MSc programme, by Maxence Bonnici, Maxence Laporte, Matéo Salvy, Meriem Boussaid and Federico Suarez. Version 2 (2026) is a complete redesign and rewrite by Maxence Bonnici: new stack, new data provider, bilingual, accessible and self-hosted. Like a printed daily, the masthead shows the volume (II, the second edition) and the issue number, which grows by one every day since the first edition on 1 December 2023.
about.stack: Next.js and React for the newspaper, Node.js with Express for the API, MariaDB for storage, all running in Docker containers on a self-hosted server in France.
about.disclaimer: Kryptonews reports information only. Nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell any asset.
